question.text:
3
A smooth field G on R \ {0} is divergence free and has outward flux one through the unit sphere.
Can a smooth field A on the same whole domain satisfy ∇ × A = G?
(A) Yes, because every divergence-free field is a curl globally.
(B) Yes, because the sphere has no boundary.
(C) No, because Stokes would make the flux of this curl through the closed sphere zero.
(D) No, because a divergence-free field cannot have nonzero flux through any sphere in its
domain.
(E) Only if A is constant.

solution.text:
If such A existed, it would be defined on a neighborhood of the sphere. Stokes's theorem
on this closed surface, whose boundary is empty, would give zero curl flux, contradicting
the given value one. Divergence-free is a local necessary condition for a vector potential,
but this domain has a global flux obstruction. Applying the divergence theorem to the
missing-origin ball would be invalid.

question.text:
3
A smooth vector field is defined on all of R . What is the flux of its curl through any smooth
closed oriented surface?
(A) It need not have a fixed value.
(B) The surface area
(C) The enclosed volume
(D) 0
(E) The circulation around a great circle

solution.text:
A closed surface has empty boundary, so Stokes’s theorem gives zero. Equivalently, the
divergence theorem and the identity ∇ · (∇ × F) = 0 yield the same conclusion.
